_comment: Curated, publicly traded 13F institutional filers. Every CIK is resolved live at run time - never a hand-typed CIK - so a wrong or delisted ticker degrades to 'no data for this manager' rather than silently reading a different filer's holdings under this name. Necessarily partial: large, influential 13F filers that are privately held (Renaissance Technologies, Citadel Advisors, Bridgewater, ...) have no ticker and are not reachable this way. Expand by adding tickers and names, not CIKs.
_filer_comment: The ticker resolves to the CIK of the *listed operating company*, and for an asset manager that is usually the entity that files the 10-K, not the one that files the 13F - those are separate registrants (T. Rowe Price Group vs. its adviser subsidiaries). build_institutional_screen.resolve_filer_ciks therefore tries the ticker's CIK first and then searches EDGAR by company name, keeping only entities whose EDGAR conformed name token-matches 'name' (or an alias) AND that actually file 13F-HRs. EDGAR's company search is a prefix match, so an adviser filed under a reordered name is unreachable from the colloquial spelling: give those managers a 'filer_aliases' list of name prefixes to search as well (for example "PRICE T ROWE"). Aliases are names, still verified against EDGAR - not CIKs, which is what keeps a typo from reading another manager's holdings under this label. The published screen's 'manager_coverage' reports, per manager, which CIKs resolved and why any resolved to none; that is the place to look before adding an alias.
_style_comment: 'style' matters because it is not a random subset of institutional flow. The largest managers here (BlackRock, State Street, Invesco) run AUM dominated by index funds and ETFs - their quarter-over-quarter position changes are close to mechanically determined by index membership and fund flows, not conviction, and feeding that into a research score that already carries valuation and sector-percentile inputs would partly reintroduce market-cap/size as a hidden second input under a 'smart money' label. build_institutional_screen.py defaults to style=active only for exactly this reason. 'alternative' (private-equity/alternative-asset managers) is excluded from the default sleeve too: their public-equity 13F stakes are typically residual holdings from take-privates or specific strategic positions, lumpy and idiosyncratic rather than a portfolio-flow signal comparable to a mutual-fund manager's.

managers.name: T. Rowe Price
managers._note: The ticker's own CIK ('PRICE T ROWE GROUP INC') is the listed holding company and files no 13F-HR. Its investment-management subsidiary was reorganized in 2023 under a new SEC registrant, T. Rowe Price Investment Management, Inc. - added as an alias so the search reaches it; verify against manager_coverage after the next run and correct if EDGAR's conformed name differs.

managers.name: Affiliated Managers Group
managers._note: AMG is a multi-affiliate holding company - its equity affiliates (AQR, Yacktman, and others) file 13Fs, if at all, under their own independent names, not under any name derived from 'Affiliated Managers Group'. No single filer_aliases entry can reach a multi-affiliate structure like this; manager_coverage will keep reporting 'files no 13F-HR' on the holding company's own CIK until this entry names one specific affiliate instead of the parent.

managers.name: Janus Henderson
managers._note: The JHG ticker itself does not resolve to a CIK in SEC's company_tickers.json (JHG is UK-domiciled and dual-listed). manager_coverage has shown search candidates rejected for a name mismatch with no conformed name captured, which points at a submissions-payload read issue on those specific CIKs rather than a wrong alias - worth checking company_search results directly against EDGAR before adding more aliases blindly.

managers.name: Virtus Investment Partners
managers._note: Virtus is also a multi-affiliate structure (Kayne Anderson Rudnick, Newfleet, Duff & Phelps, and others each run their own book); the parent's own CIK files no 13F-HR. Same limitation as AMG - a filer_aliases list keyed on 'Virtus' cannot reach affiliate-level filers.

managers.name: Artisan Partners
managers._note: The only 13F-HR filer this resolves to (CIK 0001010643) stopped filing after 2011 - likely a legacy entity superseded when Artisan Partners went public in 2013. The current operating filer is believed to be 'Artisan Partners Limited Partnership' under a different CIK; needs a live EDGAR company search to confirm the current conformed name before this can resolve to real, current holdings.

managers.name: AllianceBernstein
managers._note: The ticker's own CIK ('ALLIANCEBERNSTEIN HOLDING L.P.') is the publicly traded holding LP and files no 13F-HR; the operating LP that actually manages assets and files 13Fs is a separate registrant. It may still be registered under AllianceBernstein's pre-2000 legal name from before the Alliance Capital / Sanford Bernstein merger - added as an alias to widen the search; verify against manager_coverage.
